 --> SBI shares gain nearly 2% after Q2 results; Nomura cuts target price to Rs 1,100
 SBI reported a 14.3% year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 23,038 crore for Q2FY27 
 Moneycontrol News 
 November 05, 2026 / 12:47 IST Share --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 --> 
 SBI's profit after tax, adjusted for the stake sale, stood at Rs 170 billion, 7% below Nomura's estimate SBI shares gained nearly 2% following Q2 earnings.
 Standalone net profit rose 14.3% YoY to Rs 23,038 crore.
 Loan loss provisions declined 33% improving asset quality.

 Shares of State Bank of India (SBI) gained nearly 2% on Thursday after the country's largest lender reported its September quarter earnings, with a rise in net interest income and lower loan loss provisions supporting its profitability.
 The stock was trading at Rs 998.15, up Rs 19.15 or 1.96%, on the NSE at 12:35 pm.
 SBI reported a 14.3% year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 23,038 crore for Q2FY27. Net interest income rose 14.7% to Rs 49,143 crore, while net interest margin improved to 3.1% from just over 3% a year ago. Loan loss provisions declined 33% to Rs 2,759 crore, reflecting an improvement in asset quality.
 However, operating profit rose a relatively modest 7.3% to Rs 34,226 crore, as other income declined 24% to Rs 11,777 crore.
 SBI chairman CS Setty reiterated the bank's guidance of 10-11% deposit growth and 14-15% credit growth for FY27. He said the bank had a corporate loan pipeline of Rs 7.8 lakh crore and did not face any immediate need to raise deposit rates, given its comfortable liquidity position.

 Meanwhile, Nomura maintained its 'Neutral' rating on SBI but cut its target price to Rs 1,100 from Rs 1,160 following the Q2 results. The brokerage said higher operating expenses and treasury losses offset stronger net interest income.
 SBI's profit after tax, adjusted for the stake sale, stood at Rs 170 billion, 7% below Nomura's estimate. While NII beat estimates by 2%, operating expenses were 3% higher than expected and the treasury book reported a loss of Rs 12.8 billion.
 Nomura also flagged relatively modest underlying loan growth of 1.6% quarter-on-quarter, excluding FCNR(B)-linked loans. It expects the improvement in net interest margins in FY28 to be largely offset by higher credit costs arising from the expected transition to the expected credit loss (ECL) framework from April 2027.
